diagnostic_evidence.quote: The penultimate inequality follows from the approximation property of the local $L^2$ projection $\widehat{P}$ on $\widehat{V}_{h,k}$
Combining (\ref{eq3.2}), (\ref{eq3.3}) and the definition of the DG norm yields the estimates (\ref{eq3.1}).

issues.failure_explanation: The chain in (3.3) infers $\|\llbracket\hat{\tilde I}-\widehat P\hat{\tilde I}\rrbracket\|_{L^2(\partial\widehat K)} \lesssim h^{-1/2}\|\hat{\tilde I}-\widehat P\hat{\tilde I}\|_{H^{k+1}} \lesssim h^{k+1}\|\hat{\tilde I}\|_{H^{k+1}}$. The second estimate requires $\|v-\widehat P v\|_{H^{k+1}}\lesssim h^{k+1}\|v\|_{H^{k+1}}$, which is false: $D^{k+1}(v-\widehat P v)=D^{k+1}v$, so the $H^{k+1}$ norm of the projection error carries no $h^{k+1}$ decay. Hence the displayed inference fails and does not establish the jump bound used for (3.1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the middle step by the standard scaled trace inequality $\|w\|_{L^2(\partial\widehat K)}\lesssim h^{-1/2}\|w\|_{L^2(\widehat K)}+h^{1/2}\|w\|_{H^1(\widehat K)}$ applied to $w=\hat{\tilde I}-\widehat P\hat{\tilde I}$, using the already-invoked $L^2$/$H^1$ projection error estimates; (3.1) is then proved verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The written proof of Lemma 3.1 (and its estimate (3.1), quoted by Theorem 3.1) is invalid as written; the statement itself is standard and recoverable.
issues.title: Invalid H^{k+1}-norm trace step in the proof of Lemma 3.1
issues.why_classification: A local, routine repair (norm substitution plus a standard already-cited estimate) revalidates the same conclusion; no rate, claim, or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: L4 pairs the test-function jump with the exterior trace $(\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I)^-$ on interior inflow faces. The DG norm contains only the volume $L^2$ norm, traces on the physical boundary $\Gamma_h$, and interior jumps; it gives no control of individual exterior traces on interior faces (for a general broken function the weighted trace exceeds the DG norm by a factor $h^{-1/2}$). The claimed one-line Cauchy-Schwarz step therefore does not establish (3.4); establishing it for this specific projection error requires a nontrivial elementwise trace estimate for the $L^2$-projection error that the source does not provide (and the bound with $\|e\|_{DG}$ on the right is not available in this generality).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a contained lemma bounding the face traces of the projection error, $\sum_F\int_F|\Omega\cdot n_h||e^{\pm}|^2\lesssim h^{2k+1}\|\tilde I\|^2_{H^{k+1}}$ (via the geometric-mean trace estimate), and restate Lemma 3.2 with this right-hand side (or with the DG norm augmented by face traces); Theorem 3.1's final estimate is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.2 is unproved as stated; Theorem 3.1's decomposition (3.19), which invokes Lemma 3.2, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Interior-face term L4 not controlled by the DG norm in Lemma 3.2
issues.why_classification: A contained but genuinely nontrivial new argument (a projection-trace lemma) is required; a comparable statement suffices and the main theorem's conclusion survives, so the loss is limited.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inequality $\|\tilde I-\tilde I\circ\Phi_h^{-1}\|^2_{L^2}\le\|id-\Phi_h^{-1}\|^2_{L^\infty}\|\tilde I\|^2_{L^2}$ is false: a pointwise displacement bound controls function values only through the gradient, $\|\tilde I-\tilde I\circ\Phi_h^{-1}\|_{L^2}\lesssim\|\nabla\tilde I\|_{L^2}\,\|id-\Phi_h^{-1}\|_{L^\infty}$. For $\tilde I_\varepsilon=\varepsilon\sin(x/\varepsilon)$ the left side is $O(h^{k+1})$ while the claimed right side is $O(h^{k+1}\varepsilon)$, arbitrarily smaller. Consequently (3.9) fails, and the $\|\tilde I\|_{L^2}$-form of (3.8) (and of the $\|\tilde I- I^\dag\|^2_{L^2(\mathcal E_h)}$ step in (3.11)) is unestablished; repairing it introduces an $H^1$ (gradient) norm that must be removed by an interpolation argument absent from the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound $\|\tilde I-\tilde I\circ\Phi_h^{-1}\|_{L^2}\lesssim h^{k+1}\|\nabla\tilde I\|_{L^2}$ via the change of variables, then absorb $h^{k+1}\|\tilde I\|_{H^1}\le h^{k+1/2}\|\tilde I\|_{L^2}+h^{k+3/2}\|\tilde I\|_{H^2}$ by standard interpolation; (3.8) and all downstream uses remain valid with the same rate.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.3's estimate (3.8), as stated with the $L^2$ norm, is not proved; its use for the boundary term $T_1$ in Theorem 3.1 inherits the gap.
issues.title: False L^2-norm bound for the mapping difference in Lemma 3.3
issues.why_classification: Short local repair (correct norm plus a standard interpolation step) revalidates the identical estimate and rate; no result or guarantee is weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We consider a bounded curved domain $D \subset \mathbb{R}^d(d=2,3)$ with a Lipschitz continuous and piecewise $C^{k+1}$ smooth boundary $\Gamma$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper treats $d=2,3$. In two dimensions a boundary face $F$ is a curve, so $\Gamma^0_F=f|_F^{-1}(0)$ is a finite set of points, not 'a finite union of $C^1$ one-dimensional submanifolds', and the tubular-coordinate integration $dS=J(s,r)\,ds\,dr$ over a one-dimensional level set used to derive (3.13.5)-(3.13) is inapplicable. The written proof establishes (3.12) only for $d=3$, while the lemma (and the theory) claim it for $d=2,3$.

failure_location.quote: Consequently, the zero level set $\Gamma^0_F := f|_F^{-1}(0)$, when non-empty, is a finite union of $C^1$ one-dimensional submanifolds in $F$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the two-dimensional analogue of the argument (zero-dimensional level sets; total length of $\{|f|\lesssim h^k\}$ on each edge bounded by $\lesssim h^k$ per simple zero using (A2)); the conclusion (3.12) holds unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The tube estimate (3.12) is unproved in the 2D regime; Lemma 3.5, the second part of Lemma 3.6, and the two-dimensional case of Theorem 3.1 inherit the gap.
issues.title: Proof of Lemma 3.4 covers only three-dimensional boundary faces
issues.why_classification: Routine adaptation of the same (easier) argument to the missing regime; all claims, rates and dependents survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that there exist two positive constants $m$ and $M$ such that $0<m\leq\sigma\leq M$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof converts $L^2$ control into DG-norm control (e.g. $\|v_h\|_{L^2}\le\sigma^{-1/2}\|v_h\|_{DG}$ in (3.7) and (3.25), and the use of $\mathcal B(w,w)=\|w\|^2_{DG}$ with the stability Lemma 2.1), which requires $0<m\le\sigma\le M$. This hypothesis is stated in Lemma 2.1 but is absent from Theorem 3.1's list of assumptions, so the estimate (3.18) is not established under the hypotheses as stated.

failure_location.quote: Suppose that the assumptions $(H_1\sim H_3)$ and $(A_1\sim A_2)$ hold. Then for any $k\geq 2$, there holds

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis 'there exist $m,M>0$ with $0<m\le\sigma\le M$' to Theorem 3.1 (as in Lemma 2.1); no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.1 (and the norm conversions in Lemma 3.2's proof) are unsupported for coefficients without a positive lower bound and a finite upper bound.
issues.title: Theorem 3.1 omits the hypothesis bounding the absorption coefficient
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local condition restores the result with identical conclusion, rate and scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $I$ be the solution of (\ref{eq1.1}), and $\tilde{I}\in H^{k+1}(\mathcal{T}_h)\cap W^{1,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)$ denotes its regular extension to the computational domain.
Let $f_h\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)$ and $I_h$ be the numerical solution of (\ref{eq2.4}).

issues.failure_explanation: Estimate (3.23) combines (2.2) with $\|\tilde f-\tilde f\circ\Phi_h^{-1}\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim h^{k+1}\|\nabla\tilde f\|_{L^\infty}$, which requires $\tilde f=\Omega\cdot\nabla\tilde I+\sigma\tilde I\in W^{1,\infty}$, i.e. $W^{2,\infty}$ regularity of the extension. The theorem assumes only $\tilde I\in H^{k+1}\cap W^{1,\infty}$ and $f_h\in W^{1,\infty}$; on $D_h\setminus D$ the function $\tilde f$ is whatever the arbitrary extension produces, and its $W^{1,\infty}$ norm is neither hypothesized nor controlled by $\|f_h\|_{W^{1,\infty}}$. The displayed estimate is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the extension satisfies $\tilde f\in W^{1,\infty}$ (e.g. $\tilde I\in W^{2,\infty}$ on the boundary layer), or bound $E_1$ directly through $\tilde f\circ\Phi_h^{-1}=f_h$ under a matching $W^{1,\infty}$ assumption on $f$; the stated estimate survives.
issues.overall_effect: The $h^{k+1}\|f_h\|_{W^{1,\infty}}$ contribution to (3.18) is unestablished as written.
issues.title: E1 estimate uses an unestablished W^{1,\infty} bound on the extended source
issues.why_classification: Restoring a missing standard regularity hypothesis is routine; the theorem's conclusion, rate and scope are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Estimate (3.8) is the mapping-error bound of Lemma 3.3 and contains no information about volumes of element layers; the asserted bound $Vol(D_c)\lesssim h^{k+1}$ is a non sequitur. In fact $D_c$ (elements whose boundary meets the codimension-one characteristic set $\Gamma^0_h$) is a boundary layer of volume $\sim h^{d-1}\approx h^2$, which violates $\lesssim h^{k+1}$ for every $k\ge 2$. The subsequent chain in (3.25) that produces the $T_3$ bound is therefore unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bypass the volume route: by Lemma 3.6, $|\Omega\cdot n_h|\lesssim h^k$ on $\Gamma^-_h\Delta\Phi_h(\Gamma^-)$, and by Lemmas 3.4-3.5 that set has area $\lesssim h^k$; a weighted Cauchy-Schwarz over $S=\Gamma^-_h\Delta\Phi_h(\Gamma^-)$ gives $T_3\lesssim h^k\|\tilde I\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\|v_h\|_{DG}$ (the weighted trace of $v_h$ is part of $\|v_h\|_{DG}$), which is even stronger than what (3.18) requires.
issues.overall_effect: The $T_3$ estimate in (3.25), and hence the consistency-error contribution to (3.18), is unestablished as written.
issues.title: Unsupported volume bound Vol(D_c) ≲ h^{k+1} in the T3 estimate
issues.why_classification: A short local bypass assembled entirely from lemmas already proved in the paper preserves the final estimate (3.18) and every advertised claim; no new lemma, construction, or loss of rate is needed.
